title: The three suspects: the query, the schema and the machine

videos.script: A page takes four seconds to load, and somebody says the database is slow. {{complaint}} That sentence is almost never wrong and almost never useful. It names a building, not a culprit. {{building}} When a database answers slowly, there are three suspects. The query may ask for more work than it needs. The schema may lack the structure that would make the work small. Or the machine may be short of something: memory, disk, processors. {{suspects}} Each one has its own fix, and the fixes do not transfer. An index does nothing for a machine that is out of memory. A bigger machine does nothing for a query that reads two million rows to count forty. {{transfer}} So this course starts with a habit, not a technique. Before you change anything, you find out which suspect it is. You measure, you read what the server did, and only then you touch something. {{habit}} To do that you need a database worth measuring, and this lesson builds one on your own machine. Two million orders, five million events, and a few mistakes made on purpose. {{market}} By the end of it you will have watched the same kind of query be slow for each of the three reasons, and fast again for three different ones. {{title}}
